To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gut microbiota controls adiposity, glucose homeostasis and gut permeability via mechanisms that involve the apelinergic, endocannabinoid and enteroendocrine systems.
the gut microbiota controls gut permeability, gut hormone secretion and adipose tissue expansion via the endocannabinoids system and the apeliinergic system.
the composition of the microbiota, and in particular the relative abundance of Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes phyla, are associated with the development of metabolic disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel therapeutic strategies for the prevention and treatment of metabolic disorders, such as obesity, type 2-diabetes and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
the identification of novel molecular targets and interventions to prevent or treat obesity and associated disorders.
the identification of novel mechanisms linking the gut-to-periphery axis with the control of metabolic homeostasis and the development of metabolic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gut microbiota controls adipocyte expansion, gut barrier function, and glucose metabolism via the gut-to-periphery axis.
the gut microbiota controls the expansion of adipose tissue, gut barrier and insulin sensitivity.
the gut microbiota is a key factor in the control of energy balance and glucose homeostases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

gut microbiota and its metabolites control the gut barrier function and the gut-to-periphery communication, which are key factors involved in the onset of metabolic disorders such as obesity, type 2-diabetes and metabolic inflammation.
gut microbiota, via its metabolites, controls the development of metabolic diseases.
prebiotic intake could be used as a novel strategy to improve the metabolic status of obese subjects.

the gut microbiota is a crucial player in the development of obesity, insulin resistance, type-2 diabetes and metabolic endotoxemia.
